253: /// Drive the authorization-code flow with S256 PKCE against the candidate
254: /// issuer, through the REAL CommonCal consent flow:
255: ///   auth host -> CommonCal /consent (login decided via session)
256: ///   -> auth host -> CommonCal /consent (consent page rendered)
257: ///   -> POST /consent/decision (approve|deny) -> auth host -> loopback callback
258: ///
259: /// `decision` is "approve" or "deny". Returns (code, state) on approve;
260: /// returns Err on deny (the callback carries an error, not a code).
261: async fn authorize(
262:     ctx: &Ctx,
263:     client_id: &str,
264:     redirect: &str,
265:     scopes: &[String],
266:     resource: &str,
267:     challenge: &str,
268:     state: &str,
269:     decision: &str,
270: ) -> Result<(String, String), String> {
271:     let mut auth_url =
272:         url::Url::parse(&format!("{}/auth", ctx.cfg.issuer)).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
273:     auth_url
274:         .query_pairs_mut()
275:         .clear()
276:         .append_pair("client_id", client_id)
277:         .append_pair("redirect_uri", redirect)
278:         .append_pair("response_type", "code")
279:         .append_pair("scope", &scopes.join(" "))
280:         .append_pair("state", state)
281:         .append_pair("code_challenge", challenge)
282:         .append_pair("code_challenge_method", "S256")
283:         .append_pair("resource", resource)
284:         // The provider strips `offline_access` unless the request explicitly
285:         // asks for the consent prompt (check_scope.js). We always want a
286:         // refresh token for the P8/P9/P10 proofs, so request consent.
287:         .append_pair("prompt", "consent");
288: 
289:     // Shared cookie jar (Arc<Jar>) so the login session cookie is presented on
290:     // the consent page. The login client does NOT follow redirects (the 303 to
291:     // `/` would 404 and mask the real login status); the follow client does.
292:     let shared_jar = std::sync::Arc::new(reqwest::cookie::Jar::default());
293: 
294:     let login_client = reqwest::Client::builder()
295:         .timeout(Duration::from_secs(20))
296:         .redirect(reqwest::redirect::Policy::none())
297:         .cookie_provider(shared_jar.clone())
298:         .build()
299:         .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
300: 
301:     let follow_client = reqwest::Client::builder()
302:         .timeout(Duration::from_secs(20))
303:         .redirect(reqwest::redirect::Policy::limited(15))
304:         .cookie_provider(shared_jar.clone())
305:         .build()
306:         .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
307: 
308:     // Step 1: Login to CommonCal (sets the session cookie in the shared jar).
309:     let commoncal_base = ctx.commoncal_base();
310:     let login_resp = login_client
311:         .post(format!("{commoncal_base}/login"))
312:         .form(&[
313:             ("email", "lab@commoncal.test"),
314:             ("password", "lab-password-123"),
315:             ("continue", "/"),
316:         ])
317:         .send()
318:         .await
319:         .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
320:     let login_status = login_resp.status();
321:     if !login_status.is_success() && login_status.as_u16() != 303 {
322:         let body = login_resp.text().await.unwrap_or_default();
323:         return Err(format!(
324:             "CommonCal login failed: {login_status} at {commoncal_base}/login body={body}"
325:         ));
326:     }
327: 
328:     // Step 2: Start the authorization flow. Follow redirects until we reach
329:     // the consent page (200 HTML) or the final callback.
330:     let resp = follow_client
331:         .get(auth_url)
332:         .send()
333:         .await
334:         .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
335:     let content_type = resp
336:         .headers()
337:         .get("content-type")
338:         .and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok())
339:         .unwrap_or("")
340:         .to_string();
341:     let status = resp.status();
342:     let final_url = resp.url().to_string();
343:     let body = resp.text().await.unwrap_or_default();
344: 
345:     // If we landed on the consent page (HTML), parse the CSRF + handoff and
346:     // POST the decision.
347:     if content_type.contains("text/html") && body.contains("consent/decision") {
348:         let handoff = extract_html_value(&body, "handoff")
349:             .ok_or_else(|| "consent page missing handoff".to_string())?;
350:         let csrf = extract_html_value(&body, "csrf")
351:             .ok_or_else(|| "consent page missing csrf".to_string())?;
352: 
353:         let decision_resp = follow_client
354:             .post(format!("{commoncal_base}/consent/decision"))
355:             .form(&[
356:                 ("handoff", handoff.as_str()),
357:                 ("csrf", csrf.as_str()),
358:                 ("decision", decision),
359:             ])
360:             .send()
361:             .await
362:             .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
363:         // The decision POST returns a 303; reqwest follows the redirect chain
364:         // to the final callback (or an error page).
365:         let final_url = decision_resp.url().to_string();
366:         let final_status = decision_resp.status();
367:         let _ = decision_resp.text().await;
368: 
369:         // The final response should be the loopback callback (or an error).
370:         let cb = url::Url::parse(&final_url).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
371:         let mut code = None;
372:         let mut state_out = None;
373:         for (k, v) in cb.query_pairs() {
374:             match k.as_ref() {
375:                 "code" => code = Some(v.into_owned()),
376:                 "state" => state_out = Some(v.into_owned()),
377:                 "error" => {
378:                     let desc = cb
379:                         .query_pairs()
380:                         .find(|(kk, _)| kk.as_ref() == "error_description")
381:                         .map(|(_, vv)| vv.into_owned())
382:                         .unwrap_or_default();
383:                     return Err(format!("authorization error at {final_url}: {desc}"));
384:                 }
385:                 _ => {}
386:             }
387:         }
388:         let code = code
389:             .ok_or_else(|| format!("callback missing code (status={final_status}): {final_url}"))?;
390:         let state_out = state_out.ok_or_else(|| {
391:             format!("callback missing state (status={final_status}): {final_url}")
392:         })?;
393:         if state_out != state {
394:             return Err(format!("state mismatch: sent {state}, got {state_out}"));
395:         }
396:         return Ok((code, state_out));
397:     }
398: 
399:     // If we didn't land on the consent page, check if we got the callback
400:     // directly (e.g., the consent was auto-decided).
401:     let cb = url::Url::parse(&final_url).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
402:     let mut code = None;
403:     let mut state_out = None;
404:     for (k, v) in cb.query_pairs() {
405:         match k.as_ref() {
406:             "code" => code = Some(v.into_owned()),
407:             "state" => state_out = Some(v.into_owned()),
408:             "error" => {
409:                 let desc = cb
410:                     .query_pairs()
411:                     .find(|(kk, _)| kk.as_ref() == "error_description")
412:                     .map(|(_, vv)| vv.into_owned())
413:                     .unwrap_or_default();
414:                 return Err(format!("authorization error at {final_url}: {desc}"));
415:             }
416:             _ => {}
417:         }
418:     }
419:     let code =
420:         code.ok_or_else(|| format!("callback missing code (status={status}): {final_url}"))?;
421:     let state_out = state_out
422:         .ok_or_else(|| format!("callback missing state (status={status}): {final_url}"))?;
423:     if state_out != state {
424:         return Err(format!("state mismatch: sent {state}, got {state_out}"));
425:     }
426:     Ok((code, state_out))
427: }

429: /// Extract a hidden input value from an HTML consent page.
430: /// Looks for: <input type="hidden" name="NAME" value="VALUE">
431: fn extract_html_value(html: &str, name: &str) -> Option<String> {
432:     let needle = format!("name=\"{name}\" value=\"");
433:     let start = html.find(&needle)? + needle.len();
434:     let end = html[start..].find('"')? + start;
435:     Some(html[start..end].to_string())
436: }

438: /// Exchange the authorization code for tokens. `resource` is the exact RFC 8707
439: /// resource (sent again at token exchange to prove the provider enforces it).
440: async fn token_exchange(
441:     ctx: &Ctx,
442:     client_id: &str,
443:     redirect: &str,
444:     code: &str,
445:     verifier: &str,
446:     resource: &str,
447: ) -> Result<Value, String> {
448:     let url = format!("{}/token", ctx.cfg.issuer);
449:     let form = [
450:         ("grant_type", "authorization_code"),
451:         ("code", code),
452:         ("redirect_uri", redirect),
453:         ("client_id", client_id),
454:         ("code_verifier", verifier),
455:         ("resource", resource),
456:     ];
457:     let resp = ctx
458:         .http
459:         .post(&url)
460:         .form(&form)
461:         .send()
462:         .await
463:         .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
464:     let status = resp.status();
465:     let body: Value = resp.json().await.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
466:     if !status.is_success() {
467:         return Err(format!("token {status}: {}", err_of(&body)));
468:     }
469:     Ok(body)
470: }

518: /// Parse an MCP Streamable-HTTP response body. Handles both `application/json`
519: /// and `text/event-stream` (SSE). For SSE, returns the first `data:` payload
520: /// that is a JSON-RPC response (has `jsonrpc`/`result`/`error`).
521: fn parse_mcp_body(content_type: &str, body: &str) -> Value {
522:     if content_type.contains("text/event-stream") {
523:         for line in body.lines() {
524:             let Some(data) = line.strip_prefix("data:") else {
525:                 continue;
526:             };
527:             let data = data.trim();
528:             if data.is_empty() {
529:                 continue;
530:             }
531:             if let Ok(v) = serde_json::from_str::<Value>(data) {
532:                 if v.get("jsonrpc").is_some()
533:                     || v.get("result").is_some()
534:                     || v.get("error").is_some()
535:                 {
536:                     return v;
537:                 }
538:             }
539:         }
540:         Value::Null
541:     } else {
542:         serde_json::from_str(body).unwrap_or(Value::Null)
543:     }
544: }
545: 
546: /// One MCP Streamable-HTTP request. `token` is the RAW access token (no
547: /// "Bearer " prefix). `session` is the `mcp-session-id` from a prior response
548: /// (required after initialize). `id` is `None` for notifications. Returns
549: /// (status, parsed JSON-RPC body, session-id from the response headers).
550: async fn mcp_request(
551:     ctx: &Ctx,
552:     token: Option<&str>,
553:     session: Option<&str>,
554:     id: Option<u32>,
555:     method: &str,
556:     params: Value,
557: ) -> Result<(reqwest::StatusCode, Value, Option<String>), String> {
558:     let mcp = format!("{}/mcp", ctx.cfg.mcp_echo);
559:     let body = match id {
560:         Some(i) => json!({ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": i, "method": method, "params": params }),
561:         None => json!({ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": method, "params": params }),
562:     };
563:     let mut req = ctx
564:         .http
565:         .post(&mcp)
566:         .header("Content-Type", "application/json")
567:         .header("Accept", "application/json, text/event-stream")
568:         .json(&body);
569:     if let Some(t) = token {
570:         req = req.header("Authorization", format!("Bearer {t}"));
571:     }
572:     if let Some(s) = session {
573:         req = req.header("mcp-session-id", s);
574:     }
575:     let resp = req.send().await.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
576:     let status = resp.status();
577:     let session_id = resp
578:         .headers()
579:         .get("mcp-session-id")
580:         .and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok())
581:         .map(|s| s.to_string());
582:     let content_type = resp
583:         .headers()

1095: /// Obtain a fresh token (for MCP / refresh / revocation proofs).
1096: async fn fresh_tokens(ctx: &mut Ctx) -> Option<(String, Value)> {
1097:     let redirect = ctx.cfg.loopback_redirect.clone();
1098:     let resource = ctx.cfg.resource_url.clone();
1099:     // Request the catalog (resource) scopes plus offline_access (OIDC) so a
1100:     // refresh token is issued — needed by the P8/P9/P10 proofs.
1101:     let mut scopes: Vec<String> = SCOPE_CATALOG.iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();
1102:     scopes.push("offline_access".to_string());
1103:     let (client_id, _) = match dcr_register(ctx, &redirect).await {
1104:         Ok(v) => v,
1105:         Err(e) => {
1106:             ctx.bad("setup", &format!("DCR failed: {e}"));
1107:             return None;
1108:         }
1109:     };
1110:     let verifier = pkce_verifier();
1111:     let challenge = pkce_challenge(&verifier);
1112:     let (code, _) = match authorize(
1113:         ctx,
1114:         &client_id,
1115:         &redirect,
1116:         &scopes,
1117:         &resource,
1118:         &challenge,
1119:         "fresh-state",
1120:         "approve",
1121:     )
1122:     .await
1123:     {
1124:         Ok(v) => v,
1125:         Err(e) => {
1126:             ctx.bad("setup", &format!("authorize failed: {e}"));
1127:             return None;
1128:         }
1129:     };
1130:     match token_exchange(ctx, &client_id, &redirect, &code, &verifier, &resource).await {
1131:         Ok(t) => Some((client_id, t)),
1132:         Err(e) => {
1133:             ctx.bad("setup", &format!("token exchange failed: {e}"));
1134:             None
1135:         }
1136:     }
1137: }

1139: /// P6: MCP initialize / tools/list / tools/call with a valid token.
1140: async fn mcp_prove(ctx: &mut Ctx) {
1141:     let Some((client_id, tokens)) = fresh_tokens(ctx).await else {
1142:         ctx.bad("P6", "could not obtain a token");
1143:         return;
1144:     };
1145:     let access = tokens
1146:         .get("access_token")
1147:         .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
1148:         .unwrap_or("")
1149:         .to_string();
1150:     let _ = client_id;
1151: 
1152:     // 1) initialize -> capture the mcp-session-id.
1153:     let init_params = json!({

574:     /// Parse a UTC timestamp (ISO 8601 or Unix epoch) to i64 seconds.
575:     fn parse_ts(s: &str) -> Option<i64> {
576:         if let Ok(ts) = s.parse::<i64>() {
577:             return Some(ts);
578:         }
579:         chrono::DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(s)
580:             .ok()
581:             .map(|dt| dt.timestamp())
582:     }
583: 
584:     /// Compute availability slots for a calendar in [from, to].
585:     /// A slot is "busy" if an event overlaps it, otherwise "free".
586:     /// Slots are 1-hour blocks aligned to the hour.
587:     async fn compute_availability(
588:         &self,
589:         calendar_id: i64,
590:         from: &str,
591:         to: &str,
592:     ) -> Vec<serde_json::Value> {
593:         let from_ts = Self::parse_ts(from).unwrap_or(0);
594:         let to_ts = Self::parse_ts(to).unwrap_or(0);
595:         let events: Vec<Event> = {
596:             let st = self.inner.read().await;
597:             st.events
598:                 .values()
599:                 .filter(|e| e.calendar_id == calendar_id)
600:                 .cloned()
601:                 .collect()
602:         };
603: 
604:         let mut slots = Vec::new();
605:         let mut t = from_ts;
606:         while t < to_ts {
607:             let slot_end = (t + 3600).min(to_ts);
608:             let busy = events.iter().any(|e| {
609:                 e.start_utc.is_some_and(|s| s < slot_end)
610:                     && e.end_utc.is_some_and(|en| en > t)
611:             });
612:             slots.push(serde_json::json!({
613:                 "start": t,
614:                 "end": slot_end,
615:                 "status": if busy { "busy" } else { "free" },
616:             }));
617:             t = slot_end;
618:         }
619:         slots
620:     }

631:     /// Search events in a calendar within [from, to], optionally filtered by query.
632:     async fn search_events(
633:         &self,
634:         calendar_id: i64,
635:         from: &str,
636:         to: &str,
637:         query: Option<&str>,
638:     ) -> Vec<Event> {
639:         let from_ts = Self::parse_ts(from).unwrap_or(0);
640:         let to_ts = Self::parse_ts(to).unwrap_or(0);
641:         let st = self.inner.read().await;
642:         let mut results: Vec<Event> = st
643:             .events
644:             .values()
645:             .filter(|e| e.calendar_id == calendar_id)
646:             .filter(|e| {
647:                 e.start_utc.is_some_and(|s| s >= from_ts && s <= to_ts)
648:                     || e.end_utc.is_some_and(|en| en >= from_ts && en <= to_ts)
649:             })
650:             .filter(|e| {
651:                 query.is_none_or(|q| {
652:                     let q_lower = q.to_lowercase();
653:                     e.title
654:                         .as_deref()
655:                         .is_some_and(|t| t.to_lowercase().contains(&q_lower))
656:                         || e.description
657:                             .as_deref()
658:                             .is_some_and(|d| d.to_lowercase().contains(&q_lower))
659:                 })
660:             })
661:             .cloned()
662:             .collect();
663:         drop(st);
664:         results.sort_by_key(|e| e.start_utc.unwrap_or(0));
665:         results
666:     }

862:     /// Look up a handoff from the auth server's private API.
863:     async fn lookup_interaction(&self, handoff: &str) -> Result<InteractionView, String> {
864:         let url = format!(
865:             "{}/internal/interactions/{}",
866:             self.auth_private_base,
867:             urlencoding::encode(handoff)
868:         );
869:         let resp = self
870:             .http
871:             .get(&url)
872:             .header("Authorization", format!("Bearer {}", self.bridge_key))
873:             .send()
874:             .await
875:             .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
876:         let status = resp.status();
877:         if !status.is_success() {
878:             let body = resp.text().await.unwrap_or_default();
879:             tracing::error!(status = %status, body = %body, "lookup_interaction failed");
880:             return Err(format!("interaction lookup failed: {status} {body}"));
881:         }
882:         let body = resp.text().await.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
883:         let view: InteractionView =
884:             serde_json::from_str(&body).map_err(|e| format!("parse interaction view: {e}"))?;
885:         Ok(view)
886:     }

888:     /// Decide a handoff (login/consent/deny) via the auth server's private API.
889:     /// `subject` is the authenticated CommonCal user id (the identity authority
890:     /// is CommonCal; the auth server binds the provider grant to this subject
891:     /// rather than a hardcoded value). Returns the resume URL.
892:     ///
893:     /// Honors the lab bridge-failure test hook: if armed, this call fails
894:     /// (simulating a bridge timeout) and the hook decrements, so a retry
895:     /// succeeds — proving grant-first / bridge-second idempotent retry.
896:     async fn decide_interaction(
897:         &self,
898:         handoff: &str,
899:         kind: &str,
900:         subject: Option<i64>,
901:     ) -> Result<String, String> {
902:         // Lab test hook: simulate a bridge failure on the next CONSENT decide
903:         // call(s). Only consent decisions are affected — the grant-first /
904:         // bridge-second ordering is a consent-path property, and login decisions
905:         // must not be disrupted (they precede the grant write).
906:         if kind == "consent" {
907:             let mut st = self.inner.write().await;
908:             if st.decide_fail_remaining > 0 {
909:                 st.decide_fail_remaining -= 1;
910:                 tracing::warn!("simulating bridge decide failure (test hook)");
911:                 return Err("simulated bridge timeout (test hook)".to_string());
912:             }
913:         }
914: 
915:         let url = format!(
916:             "{}/internal/interactions/{}",
917:             self.auth_private_base,
918:             urlencoding::encode(handoff)
919:         );
920:         let mut body = serde_json::json!({ "kind": kind });
921:         if let Some(sub) = subject {
922:             body["subject"] = serde_json::json!(sub);
923:         }
924:         let resp = self
925:             .http
926:             .put(&url)
927:             .header("Authorization", format!("Bearer {}", self.bridge_key))
928:             .json(&body)
929:             .send()
930:             .await
931:             .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
932:         let status = resp.status();
933:         if !status.is_success() {
934:             let text = resp.text().await.unwrap_or_default();
935:             tracing::error!(status = %status, text = %text, "decide_interaction failed");
936:             return Err(format!("interaction decide failed: {status} {text}"));
937:         }
938:         let result: serde_json::Value = resp.json().await.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
939:         result
940:             .get("resumeUrl")
941:             .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
942:             .map(|s| s.to_string())
943:             .ok_or_else(|| "decide response missing resumeUrl".to_string())
944:     }
945: }

960: /// GET /consent?handoff=...
961: ///
962: /// If the interaction prompt is "login" and the user has a session, decide
963: /// login immediately (redirect to resume URL). If the prompt is "consent",
964: /// render the consent page. If no session, redirect to /login.
965: async fn consent_page(
966:     State(state): State<AppState>,
967:     Query(q): Query<ConsentQuery>,
968:     headers: HeaderMap,
969: ) -> Response {
970:     let handoff = match &q.handoff {
971:         Some(h) if !h.is_empty() => h.clone(),
972:         _ => {
973:             return (
974:                 StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST,
975:                 Json(serde_json::json!({"error": "missing_handoff"})),
976:             )
977:                 .into_response();
978:         }
979:     };
980: 
981:     // Look up the interaction from the auth server.
982:     let view = match state.lookup_interaction(&handoff).await {
983:         Ok(v) => v,
984:         Err(e) => {
985:             return (
986:                 StatusCode::BAD_GATEWAY,
987:                 Json(serde_json::json!({"error": e})),
988:             )
989:                 .into_response();
990:         }
991:     };
992: 
993:     // Check if the user has a session.
994:     let session_token = extract_session_cookie(&headers);
995:     let user_id = match &session_token {
996:         Some(t) => state.get_session(t).await,
997:         None => None,
998:     };
999: 
1000:     // If no session, redirect to login with a continue param.
1001:     let continue_url = format!("/consent?handoff={}", urlencoding::encode(&handoff));
1002:     let (session_token, user_id) = match (&session_token, user_id) {
1003:         (Some(t), Some(uid)) => (t.clone(), uid),
1004:         _ => {
1005:             let location = format!("/login?continue={}", urlencoding::encode(&continue_url));
1006:             return (StatusCode::SEE_OTHER, [(header::LOCATION, location)]).into_response();
1007:         }
1008:     };
1009: 
1010:     // If the prompt is "login", decide login immediately (user is authenticated).
1011:     if view.prompt == "login" {
1012:         match state
1013:             .decide_interaction(&handoff, "login", Some(user_id))
1014:             .await
1015:         {
1016:             Ok(resume_url) => {
1017:                 return (StatusCode::SEE_OTHER, [(header::LOCATION, resume_url)]).into_response();
1018:             }
1019:             Err(e) => {
1020:                 return (
1021:                     StatusCode::BAD_GATEWAY,
1022:                     Json(serde_json::json!({"error": e})),
1023:                 )
1024:                     .into_response();
1025:             }
1026:         }
1027:     }
1028: 
1029:     // If the prompt is "consent", render the consent page.
1030:     if view.prompt == "consent" {
1031:         let csrf_token = state.create_csrf(&session_token).await;
1032:         let scopes_html: Vec<String> = view
1033:             .requested_scopes
1034:             .iter()
1035:             .map(|s| format!("<li>{}</li>", escape_html(s)))
1036:             .collect();
1037:         let html = format!(
1038:             r#"<!DOCTYPE html>
1039: <html lang="en">
1040: <head><meta charset="utf-8"><title>CommonCal — Authorize</title>
1041: <style>body{{font-family:system-ui,sans-serif;max-width:480px;margin:2rem auto;padding:0 1rem}}
1042: .card{{border:1px solid #ddd;border-radius:8px;padding:1.5rem;margin-top:1rem}}
1043: button{{padding:.5rem 1rem;margin-right:.5rem;cursor:pointer;border-radius:4px;border:1px solid #ccc}}
1044: .approve{{background:#22c55e;color:#fff;border-color:#16a34a}}
1045: .deny{{background:#fff;color:#dc2626;border-color:#dc2626}}
1046: ul{{padding-left:1.2rem}}</style></head>
1047: <body>
1048: <h1>Authorize access</h1>
1049: <div class="card">
1050: <p><strong>{}</strong> is requesting access to your CommonCal account.</p>
1051: <p>Requested permissions:</p>
1052: <ul>{}</ul>
1053: <form method="POST" action="/consent/decision">
1054: <input type="hidden" name="handoff" value="{}">
1055: <input type="hidden" name="csrf" value="{}">
1056: <button type="submit" name="decision" value="approve" class="approve">Approve</button>
1057: <button type="submit" name="decision" value="deny" class="deny">Deny</button>
1058: </form>
1059: </div>
1060: </body></html>"#,
1061:             escape_html(&view.client_name),
1062:             scopes_html.join(""),
1063:             escape_html(&handoff),
1064:             escape_html(&csrf_token),
1065:         );
1066:         return (
1067:             StatusCode::OK,
1068:             [(header::CONTENT_TYPE, "text/html; charset=utf-8")],
1069:             html,
1070:         )
1071:             .into_response();
1072:     }
1073: 
1074:     // Unknown prompt — deny.
1075:     (
1076:         StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST,
1077:         Json(serde_json::json!({"error": "unknown_prompt", "prompt": view.prompt})),
1078:     )
1079:         .into_response()
1080: }

1084: async fn login_form(State(state): State<AppState>, body: axum::body::Bytes) -> Response {
1085:     let params = parse_form(&body);
1086:     let email = params.get("email").cloned().unwrap_or_default();
1087:     let password = params.get("password").cloned().unwrap_or_default();
1088:     // Open-redirect guard: an unsafe `continue` falls back to the safe root.
1089:     let continue_url = params
1090:         .get("continue")
1091:         .and_then(|v| validate_continuation(v))
1092:         .unwrap_or_else(|| "/".to_string());
1093: 
1094:     let user = {
1095:         let st = state.inner.read().await;
1096:         st.users.get(&email).cloned()
1097:     };
1098: 
1099:     let Some(user) = user else {
1100:         return (StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED, "Invalid credentials").into_response();
1101:     };
1102:     if user.password != password {
1103:         return (StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED, "Invalid credentials").into_response();
1104:     }
1105: 
1106:     let session_token = state.create_session(user.id).await;
1107:     let set_cookie = format!(
1108:         "commoncal_session={}; Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax",
1109:         session_token
1110:     );
1111:     (
1112:         StatusCode::SEE_OTHER,
1113:         [
1114:             (header::SET_COOKIE, set_cookie),
1115:             (header::LOCATION, continue_url),
1116:         ],
1117:     )
1118:         .into_response()
1119: }

display.text:
# Connecting an agent to CommonCal MCP

## Production status

As verified on 2026-09-17, the production endpoint is reachable but is **not
currently connectable by a standard MCP client**:

- `POST https://mcal.hajnal.space/mcp` with `tools/list` returns the tool catalog.
- An MCP `initialize` request returns `-32601 Method not found`.
- Protected-resource discovery advertises `https://cal.hajnal.space` as the
  authorization server, but its OIDC discovery URL returns the CommonCal HTML
  application instead of OAuth metadata.

Both MCP initialization and OAuth discovery must be fixed before an agent can
make authenticated tool calls.

## Connect from OpenCode

OpenCode is the MCP client. LM Studio is the model provider and Qwen is the
model, so neither one connects to MCP directly. No additional MCP client needs
to be supplied. Once production is fixed, add the remote Streamable HTTP server:

```sh
opencode mcp add commoncal-production --url https://mcal.hajnal.space/mcp
```

Run `opencode mcp list`. If authentication is required, start it with:

```sh
opencode mcp auth commoncal-production
```

OpenCode can discover OAuth configuration, register a public client when the
authorization server supports dynamic registration, and manage its tokens. Do
not configure `MCP_INTERNAL_API_KEY` in the agent; that secret is only for
communication from the MCP server to CommonCal core.

OpenCode's browser OAuth flow requires a callback reachable from the user's
browser. See the [OpenCode MCP documentation](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/mcp-servers).
After authentication, verify `initialize`, `tools/list`, and `calendar_list`.

An additional MCP client is useful only for independent smoke testing, for
example MCP Inspector. It is not part of the production connection architecture.
